correctness.rationale: Every valid directed path branching is exactly L^k R^(n-k): any RL adjacent pair forms a forbidden 2-cycle, and all other orientations reach an endpoint. Direct cost-counting gives a base count plus simple symmetric partial sums. The leftmost-minimum law factors via reflection into strict and weak nonnegative walks. The expected minimum follows the exact reflection identity, binomial absolute moment and parity atom, including n=1 and odd-n central BFD tie. Donsker invariance, a.s.-unique Brownian minimum and Levy arcsine yield the tie-rule-invariant limit and 2/3 concentration. Extractable standard-library verification exhausts 65,534 rankings and 4,096 explicit rooted-orientation checks. Computation corroborates finite algebra and is not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The exact social-choice objective tradeoff is motivated by the source paper. The new reduction quantifies how saving Theta(sqrt(n)) second-choice votes under globally minimum-ranked branching produces Theta(n) asymmetry in guru weights with limiting probability 2/3; BFD instead has balanced weights. A full finite optimum-cut law, closed finite expected costs and arbitrary-optimum-tie robust asymptotic show structural mathematical information beyond a renamed textbook probability theorem or one-off example.
